name: Projected Recursive Teaching Dimension of Singletons
proof: For $n=1$, every projection has one trace and recursive teaching dimension zero. For $n\ge2$, every projection consists of singleton traces, possibly together with the empty trace. Remove singleton traces first, using their unique positive coordinates whenever competitors remain; the final trace has an empty teaching set. This is a positive recursive plan of width at most one, hence also an ordinary one. The identity projection is nontrivial, so recursive width zero is impossible.
